failures.evidence: RedirectTest.java:336,339 assert assertEquals(postOnALiveCode.body(), postOnAnUnissuedCode.body()) (and the DELETE pair). Both sides return 405 with Spring's DefaultErrorAttributes body; they differ only in the echoed request path and the millisecond timestamp: expected <{"timestamp":"...780+00:00","status":405,"error":"Method Not Allowed","path":"/PkfPFtvxisTmPSoQ1wAjyS"}> but was <..."path":"/ZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZz"}> (surefire TEST-...RedirectTest.xml, MultipleFailuresError at RedirectTest.java:333). The contract says both things: openapi.yaml:47 'Every non-2xx response has the ApiError shape. The catalogue is closed' — a table with no 405 row and no wire value a 405 could use — and openapi.yaml:123-124 note 2 'Every other method on /{code} answers 405 from Spring's own dispatcher. No operation is declared for them', repeated at openapi.yaml:589. A dispatcher-produced 405 necessarily carries path and timestamp, so byte-equal bodies at two different paths is unreachable under note 2; under line 47 the whitelabel body is out of shape, but honouring line 47 requires inventing a 405 catalogue entry the same line declares closed. AC15 (requirement.json) constrains only 'requesting a short code' and is silent on other methods; the observed 405s leak nothing about existence, differing only in caller-known path and clock. Contract behaviour B106 says 'refused identically whether or not the code resolves', without the 'byte for byte' wording B104 uses for the 404 body, so it does not settle the reading. Neither branch can be sent this without a human choosing the 405 body.

summary: One test fails out of 148 (21 classes, 0 errors): RedirectTest.aMethodOtherThanGetOrHeadIsRefusedWithoutRevealingWhetherTheCodeExists. The coverage_floor gate failure is purely downstream — surefire dies in the test phase so no JaCoCo report is written ('no JaCoCo report at .../jacoco.csv') — and routes_match_openapi passed with 8/8 routes. Everything the previous triage routed to implement and author-tests is now green; what remains is the single item that triage already classified 'contract' and that no human has ruled on. The conflict is inside openapi.yaml: line 47 promises every non-2xx has the ApiError shape from a closed catalogue containing no 405, while note 2 (line 123) and the /{code} description (line 589) hand 405 to Spring's own dispatcher, whose body embeds the request path and a timestamp and therefore cannot be byte-equal across two different codes. author-tests read line 47; implement read note 2. If I am wrong, the thing to check is whether line 47 was meant to govern the click surface at all — if a human rules that it does, this becomes an implementation defect fixable with an @ExceptionHandler(HttpRequestMethodNotSupportedException) returning a fixed body, but that needs a wire value the closed catalogue does not supply, so the catalogue gains a row either way. Do not repair by loosening the assertion to compare status only; that erases the intent without deciding the question.
